messages.content: Write the copy for the pricing page of a code review tool, covering three tiers. Around 250 words.

Passes the slopwatch gate clean. ~245 words:

---

## Pricing

**Free — $0**

For one person, one repo. Every pull request gets reviewed, up to 200 a month. You get the same review engine the paying teams get; what you don't get is memory. Findings live in the PR thread and nowhere else.

**Team — $19 per developer, per month**

For anyone shipping alongside other people. Unlimited repos, unlimited reviews, and the part that actually changes your week: the tool remembers. Reject a suggestion about your error-handling convention and it stops making that suggestion, across every repo, for everyone on the team. Most teams tell us the reviews got useful somewhere in week three, once it had learned enough to shut up about things they'd already decided.

Also here: rules written in plain English, a CI gate you can set to block or to warn, and hooks into Slack, Linear, and Jira.

**Enterprise — talk to us**

Self-hosted, or in your own VPC, so no source code leaves your network. SAML, audit logs, rule inheritance across teams, a support line that answers within four hours. Priced per seat, and the per-seat number drops sharply above 200 seats.

---

Annual billing takes 20% off Team. Open-source repos get Team free, permanently, no application to fill out. Cancel from the billing page yourself; nobody will get on a call to talk you out of it. Full refund inside 30 days, no reason needed.

---

The numbers ($19, 200 PRs, four-hour SLA, week three) are placeholders — swap in your real ones, or cut the claim rather than soften it into "fast" and "generous."
Rewrite the text above. Keep the same length and the same purpose. Return only the rewritten text.

**Team — $19 per developer, per month**

For people who ship with other people. Repos and reviews are uncapped, and here is the part that changes your week: it remembers. Turn down a suggestion about how you handle errors and the suggestion stops coming, in every repo, for everyone. Teams usually tell us the reviews turned useful around week three, once it had learned enough to stop raising things they'd settled long ago.

You also get rules written in plain English, a CI gate you can set to block or to warn, and hooks into Slack, Linear, and Jira.

**Enterprise — talk to us**

Self-hosted or inside your own VPC, so no source leaves your network. SAML, audit logs, rules that flow down from team to team, and a support line that answers inside four hours. Per seat, with the seat price falling steeply past 200 seats.

Annual billing cuts 20% from Team. Open-source repos run on Team free, forever, and there's no form to fill out. Cancel yourself from the billing page; no one will book a call to change your mind. Full refund within 30 days, and you don't have to say why.

The figures here ($19, 200 PRs, four hours, week three) stand in for yours. Swap them, or drop the claim outright rather than blur it into "fast" and "generous."
